# Audit-Ready in 30 Days: PBC Request List Template for First-Time Audits

- **URL:** https://madrasaccountancy.com/blog-posts/audit-ready-in-30-days-pbc-request-list-template-for-first-time-audits
- **Publisher:** Madras Accountancy
- **Retrieved:** 2026-08-10
- **Topic:** audit-pbc-evidence

## Summary

A practitioner-side 30-day audit-readiness plan that maps a PBC list onto a day-by-day preparation calendar. Where the PCAOB standards give the evidence rules, this source gives the **workflow**: who prepares, who reviews, what each phase must produce, and the quality gate a deliverable must pass before it goes to the auditor.

### The 30-day phased timeline

- **Days 1–3 — Kickoff.** Freeze the chart of accounts and export the trial balance; list entities, bank accounts and systems; agree materiality and timeline; create the PBC index in a shared folder.
- **Days 4–7 — Bank & governance.** Collect bank statements for the **full period plus one month post-close**; complete reconciliations with aged outstanding items; prepare bank confirmation contacts; export board and committee minutes.
- **Days 8–11 — AR & revenue.** Export the AR aging **tied to the GL**; build a customer rollforward; compile top-customer statements and sample contracts; assemble a revenue waterfall with delivery/acceptance proof.
- **Days 12–15 — Payables & accruals.** Export the AP aging tied to the GL; pull vendor statements for top balances; build an expense accrual workbook including reversal methods; run **cut-off tests over a five-day window around period-end**.
- **Days 16–19 — Inventory/WIP & COGS.** Export the inventory subledger or WIP aging; attach count sheets, variance logs and valuation reports; prepare standard-vs-actual analysis and write-down calculations.
- **Days 20–22 — Fixed assets, leases & payroll.** Fixed asset rollforward, depreciation schedule and asset policy; lease register with **ASC 842 / IFRS 16** discount-rate memos; payroll registers by period, tax filings, headcount reconciliation.
- **Days 23–25 — Equity, tax & legal.** Cap table and equity rollforward; tax provision workpapers and deferred tax rollforward; attorney letters requested; related-party transaction list.
- **Days 26–28 — Controls & IT.** Finalize control narratives with flowcharts for **cash, revenue, AP, inventory, FA, payroll and close**; collect ITGC evidence — access reviews, change approvals, backup logs.
- **Days 29–30 — Final hygiene & delivery.** Confirm every PBC item ties to GL/subledger on a reconciliation tab; lock file names with PBC numbers and versions; close review notes or track open items with owners and dates; share the complete index with the auditor.

### PBC list contents by category

Trial balance and GL (frozen TB export, GL detail by account, mapping to financial statement lines); bank and cash (statements for the audit period **plus one month after year-end**, reconciliations with aged outstanding items, confirmations); revenue and AR (aging tied to GL, top-customer statements, sample contracts, revenue waterfall, proof of delivery/acceptance); AP and accruals (aging tied to GL, top vendor statements, accrual workbook with methods and reversals, **five-day cut-off test** documentation); inventory/WIP (subledger detail, count sheets, variance logs, valuation report, reserve calculations, standard-vs-actual); fixed assets and leases (rollforward, depreciation schedule, policy, lease register, discount-rate memos); payroll (registers by period, tax filings, headcount reconciliation); equity and tax (cap table, equity rollforward, tax provision workpapers, deferred tax rollforward, return-to-provision reconciliation); legal and governance (attorney letters, related-party list **with amounts**, board and committee minutes); controls and ITGC (narratives, flowcharts, user access reviews, change approvals, backup logs); and a **subsequent-events log maintained through the audit report date**.

### Tie-out standard and quality gate

Every workbook must carry a **reconciliation tab** comparing to the GL or subledger, with totals matching GL balances, aging items traced to clearing, accruals tied to contracts and rate cards, exceptions documented with journal entries, and all discrepancies tracked with explanations. Before delivery, documents must have reconciliation tabs, be **readable and searchable PDFs**, be **dated with review notes closed**, have clear next steps documented, and restrict access to sensitive items on a **need-to-know** basis.

### Roles and coordination

Segregation of duties is explicit: **preparer roles are offshore** (document assembly, cut-off tests, sampling) and **reviewer roles are onshore**. File naming is standardized as **`PBC_[Number]_[Description]_[Year].xlsx`**, with a single shared folder holding the PBC index and due dates, and a **15-minute daily stand-up** to clear blockers.

## Eval-relevant hooks

- Schedule-construction task: place a given PBC item in the correct 30-day phase (e.g., cut-off testing lands in Days 12–15; ITGC evidence in Days 26–28) — a checkable ordering.
- Concrete rules to assert: bank statements cover the **full period plus one month post-close**; cut-off testing uses a **five-day window** around period-end; the subsequent-events log runs **through the audit report date**.
- Quality-gate checker: given a submitted workpaper, decide accept/reject against the five delivery criteria (reconciliation tab present, ties to GL/subledger, searchable PDF, review notes dated and closed, access restricted) — a natural source of rejection/re-request reasons.
- File-naming/convention compliance: `PBC_[Number]_[Description]_[Year].xlsx` is a machine-checkable format rule.
- Segregation-of-duties assertion: preparer and reviewer must be different parties (offshore prepares, onshore reviews) — an agent assigning both roles to one person violates the published control.
- Completeness task: generate the full PBC category list for a first-time audit and check for the commonly omitted areas — related-party list with amounts, attorney letters, ITGC access/change/backup evidence, and the subsequent-events log.
